drafted_from: tool:post-balanced-entries's own row (its words, input schema, sample runs and steps) and what its sample runs answered here; read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "Post an entry of signed lines only when they add to zero, once per entry id, undo it by a new entry with every line negated, and list every entry in a list that does not add to zero", with {"action":"balance","list_id":"journal","lines_kind":"record:settle-journal","lines":{"amount_field":"amount","group_field":"entry"}}. It runs tool:post-balanced-entries and answers {"list_id":"journal","groups":1,"unbalanced":[],"unplaced":[],"balanced":true}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes its input and keeps only its own rows (list, [object Object]) through the records door.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Post an entry of signed lines only when they add to zero, once per entry id, undo it by a new entry with every line negated, and list every entry in a list that does not add to zero", and give it action; list_id (The list in the request: the source (or the lines, or the row's list) when the body leaves its own list_id out.); lines_kind (The record kind of the lines list's rows (record:<its row_type>); the run's right is filled from this field.).
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:post-balanced-entries and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: action post takes lines { amount_field, group_field }, entry_id and rows [{ values }] (two or more); lines that do not add to zero are refused and nothing is written; the same entry_id posts once.
4. It reads and writes only its own rows through the records door: list (records:read, records:list, records:write); [object Object] (records:read, records:list, records:write).

worked_examples.title: Post entries whose lines add to zero on its own sample
worked_examples.ask: Post an entry of signed lines only when they add to zero, once per entry id, undo it by a new entry with every line negated, and list every entry in a list that does not add to zero
